ch.s: Verses 1–4: “O LORD Almighty in heaven, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their righteous offspring”; Verses 5–8: “for the majesty of your glory can’t be borne, and the anger of your threatening toward sinners is unbearable.”; Verses 9–12: “For I have sinned more than the number of the sands of the sea. My transgressions are multiplied, O Lord, my transgressions are multiplied, and I am not…”; Verses 13–15: “but, I humbly ask you, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and please don’t destroy me with my iniquities. Don’t be angry with me forever, by reserving evil…”. People named: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob.
q: Read verses 1–4. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–8, what do you learn about sin and repentance?
Read verse 8 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Abraham’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of grace and mercy in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Prayer of Manasseh?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.
